originalPrompt: A portable tactical radar with a touchscreen display, titanium and carbon fiber enclosure
projectDescription: Portable Tactical Radar built around a ESP32-C3 SuperMini with HLK-LD2410C 24 GHz mmWave Presence Radar, 2.8in TFT 320x240 Touch (ILI9341 + XPT2046); battery-powered (≈5.5 h per charge), housed in a Carbon Fiber PETG enclosure.
plan:
- Main Controller: ESP32-C3 SuperMini — $2.90/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Presence Radar: HLK-LD2410C 24 GHz mmWave Presence Radar — $3.90/unit; named in the prompt: radar
- Display: 2.8in TFT 320x240 Touch (ILI9341 + XPT2046) — $8.50/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Battery: LiPo 3.7 V 2000 mAh (104060, PCM) — $5.50/unit; matches rechargeable
- USB-C Charger + Protection: TP4056 USB-C Li-ion Charger + Protection — 1S Li-ion needs CC/CV charging and over-discharge protection
- 5V Boost: MT3608 Boost Converter (set 5 V) — $0.50/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Power: li-po 7.4 Wh, est. runtime 5.5 h
- Enclosure: 100×95×30 mm in Carbon Fiber PETG

nodes.name: Main Controller
nodes.description: Tiny RISC-V 160 MHz board with Wi-Fi + BLE 5, USB-C. Few GPIO; great for small sensors.
rationale: rejected: arduino-nano-every (Arduino Nano Every: not enough UART ports (0))
rejected: esp32-cam (ESP32-CAM (AI-Thinker) + OV2640 has no SPI bus)

nodes.name: Battery
rationale: 7.4 Wh vs 6.3 Wh needed for 4 h

nodes.name: USB-C Charger + Protection
rationale: 1S Li-ion needs CC/CV charging and over-discharge protection

nodes.name: 5V Boost
rationale: boost: 3–4.2 V → 5 V, 1000 mA ≥ peak 440 mA

nodes.name: Enclosure Base
nodes.description: Printed tray 100×95×30 mm, 2 mm walls, integrated M2.5 bosses.

nodes.name: Enclosure Lid
nodes.description: Lid with 1 display window(s); screws into base bosses.

nodes.name: M2.5 Brass Standoffs
rationale: lift boards 5 mm off the floor for wiring clearance

assumptions: Slicer (PrusaSlicer/Cura/Bambu Studio) configured for the listed materials
PlatformIO (VS Code extension or CLI) installed
Lithium battery safety: never short, puncture or charge unattended

subSteps.title: 3D print 2 part(s) in Carbon Fiber PETG
Test-fit boards on standoffs before wiring
Assemble the power path (battery, charger, regulators)
Solder UART bus lines to Presence Radar
Solder SPI bus lines to Display, Display
Verify continuity and rail voltages before inserting the MCU
Mount boards and modules inside the enclosure
Install panel parts (display/controls) into the lid
Close the enclosure and fasten the lid
